description: Screenshot of an online article headlined 'The Storm Is the New Pizzagate — Only Worse' by Paris Martineau (@parismartineau), dated December 19, 2017, 9:32 am — the layout matches New York Magazine's Intelligencer. The article image is an orange sunset-over-ocean graphic reading 'CALM BEFORE THE STORM' with a lion emblem, captioned as an Anonymous graphic. The opening paragraphs describe 'The Storm' conspiracy theory as a successor to Pizzagate. Chanel fashion advertisements border the page.
text: CHANEL. The Storm Is the New Pizzagate — Only Worse. By Paris Martineau. @parismartineau. December 19, 2017 9:32 am. Share. Tweet. Share. Comment. CALM BEFORE THE STORM. They have a surprisingly decent graphics department over in Crazyland. Photo: Anonymous. A new conspiracy theory called “The Storm” has taken the grimiest parts of the internet by, well, storm. Like Pizzagate, the Storm conspiracy features secret cabals, a child sex-trafficking ring led (in part) by the satanic Democratic Party, and of course, countless logical leaps and paranoid assumptions that fail to hold up under the slightest fact-based scrutiny. However, unlike Pizzagate, the Storm isn’t focused on a single block of shops in D.C., or John Podesta’s emails. It’s much, much bigger than that. As most terrible things do, this story begins with a post on /pol/, a sub. CHA. Most Viewed Stories.
flags: Article characterizes The Storm/Pizzagate as debunked conspiracy theories; the archive records the article's framing without endorsement
Outlet identified from layout as NY Mag Intelligencer — masthead not visible in the crop

description: Meme shown inside an anonymous imageboard post frame dated Dec 18 2019. A painted Vietnam War-style battle scene of soldiers firing rifles and machine guns amid jungle explosions, with each soldier's face replaced by the Pepe the Frog cartoon; a propeller aircraft flies overhead. Top and bottom captions joke that anonymous posters were 'surrounded' by 'shills' attacking from all sides.
text: Anonymous. Dec 18 2019. IT WAS HELL OUT THERE AND WE WERE SURROUNDED. THE SHILLS CAME AT US FROM ALL SIDES IN A RELENTLESS ATTACK.
flags: Pepe the Frog imagery is associated with imageboard culture and has been listed as a hate symbol in some contexts; used here as a generic mascot in a battle-scene joke

description: Photograph taken from inside the open doorway of a helicopter parked on the White House South Lawn, consistent with Marine One. A blond man in a long dark overcoat, consistent with President Donald Trump, walks across the lawn toward the West Wing colonnade where a press gaggle and staff are gathered; the Eisenhower Executive Office Building rises behind. In the foreground a suited man with an earpiece, consistent with a Secret Service agent, stands facing away beside the aircraft door.
flags: Distant figure identified as Trump from build, hair and context rather than a clear view of the face — probable, not certain
Foreground agent is a private individual and is not identified
